questions.text: What does CPU stand for?
questions.solution: CPU stands for central processing unit: it processes data and instructions
questions.hint: It is the part of the computer that does the processing

questions.text: What does RAM stand for? Give the full name.

feedback.read only memory: Read only memory is ROM; RAM's first word is about how data can be accessed

questions.solution: RAM stands for random access memory
questions.hint: The first word means any location can be reached directly, in any order

questions.text: Which type of memory is non-volatile and stores the instructions needed to start up the computer (the boot program)?

feedback: RAM is volatile: it loses its contents when the power is off
Cache is volatile and holds frequently used data
A register is a tiny, volatile store inside the CPU

questions.solution: ROM (read only memory) is non-volatile and holds the boot program (for example the BIOS)
questions.hint: It keeps its contents when the power is off and is normally only read

questions.text: What does it mean when memory is volatile?

options: It loses its contents when the power is turned off
It keeps its contents when the power is turned off
It can only be read, not written to
It is stored on a hard disk

questions.solution: Volatile memory, such as RAM, loses its contents when the power is turned off
questions.hint: Think about what happens to RAM when a computer is switched off

questions.text: Name the small, very fast memory inside or very close to the CPU that stores frequently used data and instructions. Give the term.
questions.solution: Cache memory is small, very fast memory that stores frequently used data and instructions near the CPU
questions.hint: It is faster than RAM but much smaller

questions.text: Which of these is an example of secondary storage?

feedback: RAM is primary storage (main memory)
Cache is part of the CPU's memory, not secondary storage
A register is inside the CPU

questions.solution: Secondary storage keeps data permanently, like an SSD, hard disk or USB drive
questions.hint: Secondary storage keeps data when the power is off

questions.text: What is the difference between RAM and ROM?

options: RAM is volatile and can be written to; ROM is non-volatile and is normally read only
RAM is non-volatile; ROM is volatile
RAM stores the boot program; ROM stores the programs that are running
RAM is secondary storage; ROM is primary storage

questions.solution: RAM is volatile and holds the programs and data in use; ROM is non-volatile and holds the boot program
questions.hint: Think about which one loses its contents when the power is off

questions.text: In the fetch-decode-execute cycle, which stage comes straight after an instruction is fetched? Give one word.

feedback.execute: The instruction has to be understood before it can be carried out
feedback.executing: The instruction has to be understood before it can be carried out

questions.solution: Fetch, then decode (work out what the instruction means), then execute
questions.hint: The name of the cycle lists the stages in order

questions.text: Which register holds the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched?

feedback: The accumulator stores the results of calculations
The MDR holds the data or instruction that has just been fetched or is about to be written
The CIR holds the instruction currently being decoded and executed

questions.solution: The program counter holds the address of the next instruction and is then increased
questions.hint: It counts through the program

questions.text: Which part of the CPU carries out arithmetic and logical operations? Give its full name or its abbreviation.

feedback.control unit: The control unit coordinates the CPU; it does not do the calculations
feedback.cu: The control unit coordinates the CPU; it does not do the calculations

questions.solution: The arithmetic logic unit (ALU) does calculations and logical comparisons
questions.hint: Its name describes the two kinds of operation it does

questions.text: Which translator converts a whole high-level program into machine code in one go, producing an executable file?

feedback: An interpreter translates and runs the program one line at a time
An assembler translates assembly language, not a high-level language
An operating system is not a translator

questions.solution: A compiler translates the whole high-level program at once and produces an executable file
questions.hint: It translates everything before any of the program runs

questions.text: Which translator translates and runs a high-level program one line at a time? Give the term.

feedback.compiler: A compiler translates the whole program in one go

questions.solution: An interpreter translates and runs one line at a time
questions.hint: Think of a person who translates a speech sentence by sentence

questions.text: Software that manages the hardware, runs other programs and provides a user interface is called what? Give the term.

feedback.utility software: Utility software does maintenance jobs, such as backup or defragmentation
feedback.utility: Utility software does maintenance jobs, such as backup or defragmentation

questions.solution: The operating system manages hardware, memory and files, runs programs and provides a user interface
questions.hint: Windows, macOS, Linux and Android are examples

questions.text: A computer is running so many programs that RAM is full. What does the operating system use so that the computer can keep running?
questions.solution: Virtual memory uses part of secondary storage as if it were extra RAM
questions.hint: Part of the hard disk or SSD is used as if it were RAM

questions.text: Which of these is a disadvantage of virtual memory?

options: It is much slower than RAM, so the computer can slow down
It deletes files from the hard disk
It lowers the CPU's clock speed

questions.solution: Virtual memory is on secondary storage, which is much slower than RAM, so moving data back and forth slows the computer
questions.hint: Where is virtual memory stored, and how fast is that?

questions.text: A photographer needs to store thousands of large image files with a large capacity at a low cost per gigabyte. Which type of secondary storage is most suitable: magnetic, optical or solid state? Give one word.

feedback.solid state: Solid state storage is fast, but it costs more per gigabyte
feedback.ssd: Solid state storage is fast, but it costs more per gigabyte
feedback.optical: Optical discs hold much less data each, so they are not suited to thousands of large files

questions.solution: Magnetic hard disk drives give a large capacity at a low cost per gigabyte
questions.hint: Think about which type is cheapest per gigabyte for a large capacity

questions.text: A games company wants its finished game to run quickly on players' computers without giving away its source code. Which translator should it use?
questions.solution: A compiler produces an executable file, which runs quickly and can be shared without the source code
questions.hint: Which translator produces a file that runs on its own?

questions.text: Which of these is a job of an operating system?
questions.solution: Managing memory is a job of the operating system; the others are done by application software
questions.hint: The operating system manages the computer's resources

questions.text: Which part of the CPU sends control signals to coordinate the fetch-decode-execute cycle? Give its full name or abbreviation.

feedback.alu: The ALU does calculations; it does not control the cycle
feedback.arithmetic logic unit: The ALU does calculations; it does not control the cycle

questions.solution: The control unit (CU) decodes instructions and sends control signals to coordinate the CPU
questions.hint: Its name says what it does: it is in charge of the CPU

questions.text: Increasing which of these usually lets a CPU carry out more instructions per second?
questions.solution: A higher clock speed means more fetch-decode-execute cycles per second
questions.hint: It is measured in gigahertz (GHz)

questions.text: CPU X has 4 cores at 3.0 GHz. CPU Y has 2 cores at 3.0 GHz, and both have the same cache. Why might CPU X not run a program twice as fast as CPU Y?

options: The program may not be able to split its work between several cores
Having more cores lowers the clock speed
More cores always halve the speed

questions.solution: Extra cores only help if the program's work can be split up and done at the same time
questions.hint: Can every program share its work between cores?

questions.text: A clock speed of 3.2 GHz means that the CPU carries out about…
questions.solution: 1 GHz is 1 billion (1 000 000 000) cycles per second, so 3.2 GHz is about 3.2 billion cycles per second
questions.hint: Giga means a billion, and hertz means per second

questions.text: In the von Neumann architecture, program instructions and data are stored together in the same place. Where? Give one word.
questions.solution: In the von Neumann architecture, instructions and data share the same memory
questions.hint: Instructions are fetched from the same place that data is read from

questions.text: Why does a larger cache usually improve CPU performance?

options: More frequently used data can be accessed quickly without fetching it from RAM

questions.solution: With more cache, more data and instructions can be read from fast cache instead of slower RAM
questions.hint: Cache is faster than RAM

questions.text: A computer slows down when many applications are open, and it keeps reading from and writing to its storage drive. Which upgrade would most likely help?
questions.solution: The computer is using virtual memory because RAM is full; more RAM means less swapping to the slower drive
questions.hint: Why would the computer use its storage drive as memory?

questions.text: Name the bus that carries memory addresses from the CPU to memory. Give the term.

feedback.data bus: The data bus carries the data itself, not the address
feedback.control bus: The control bus carries control signals, such as read and write

questions.solution: The address bus carries addresses from the CPU to memory
questions.hint: Its name says what it carries

questions.text: Which type of utility software reorganises the files on a magnetic hard disk so that the parts of each file are stored next to each other? Give the term.
questions.solution: Defragmentation software moves the scattered parts of files together, so a hard disk can read them faster
questions.hint: The parts of files become scattered (fragmented) over time

questions.text: Which statement about compilers and interpreters is accurate?

options: A compiler reports errors after translating the whole program; an interpreter stops at the first error it finds
An interpreter produces an executable file that runs without the translator
A compiled program needs the compiler every time it runs
An interpreter translates the whole program before running any of it

questions.solution: A compiler translates everything and then lists the errors; an interpreter stops as soon as it reaches an error
questions.hint: Think about when each translator finds errors

questions.text: Why is solid state storage often used in laptops and phones instead of magnetic hard disks?

options: It has no moving parts, so it is more robust and uses less power
It always has a larger capacity
It is volatile, so it is faster

questions.solution: Solid state storage has no moving parts, so it is robust when carried around, light and uses little power
questions.hint: Think about devices that get carried around and run on batteries

questions.text: Which of these is an embedded system?

options: The computer that controls a washing machine
A desktop PC used for homework
A web server in a data centre

questions.solution: An embedded system is a computer built into a larger device to do one specific job, such as controlling a washing machine
questions.hint: An embedded system is built into a device and has one dedicated job

questions.text: During the fetch stage, the address held in the program counter is copied into which register?

feedback: The MDR receives the instruction fetched from that address
The accumulator holds the results of calculations
The CIR holds the instruction after it has been fetched

questions.solution: The address in the PC is copied to the MAR, then the instruction at that address is fetched into the MDR
questions.hint: The register you need holds an address

questions.text: A program is written in a high-level language. Why must it be translated before the CPU can run it?

options: The CPU can only execute machine code
The CPU can only run interpreted programs

questions.solution: The CPU only understands machine code (binary instructions), so high-level code must be compiled or interpreted
questions.hint: What kind of instructions does the CPU understand?

questions.text: Why is defragmentation not needed for a solid state drive?

options: An SSD has no moving read/write head, so scattered data can be read just as quickly
SSDs store data on optical discs

questions.solution: An SSD reads any location equally quickly, so fragmented files do not slow it down (and defragmenting would cause extra wear)
questions.hint: Why do scattered files slow down a magnetic hard disk?

questions.text: What does LAN stand for?
questions.solution: LAN stands for local area network: a network covering a small area such as one building
questions.hint: It covers a small geographical area

questions.text: What does WAN stand for? Give the full name.

feedback.local area network: That is a LAN; a WAN covers a much larger area

questions.solution: WAN stands for wide area network: a network covering a large geographical area, such as the internet
questions.hint: It covers a large geographical area

questions.text: Which type of malware pretends to be useful software to trick users into installing it?

feedback: A worm spreads by itself across a network
A virus attaches itself to files and spreads when they are run
Spyware secretly records what a user does

questions.solution: A Trojan disguises itself as legitimate software, named after the wooden horse in the Greek story
questions.hint: It is named after a famous wooden horse

questions.text: What is phishing?

options: Sending fake emails or messages to trick people into giving away personal details
Flooding a server with traffic so it stops working
Trying every possible password until one works
Watching someone type in their PIN

questions.solution: Phishing uses fake emails or messages that look genuine to trick people into giving away details such as passwords
questions.hint: It sounds like a sport where bait is used to catch something

questions.text: What is the name for hardware or software that checks network traffic coming in and going out, and blocks traffic that breaks a set of rules? Give the term.
questions.solution: A firewall monitors incoming and outgoing traffic and blocks anything that breaks its rules
questions.hint: In a building, it is a barrier that stops a fire spreading

questions.text: What does encryption do to data?

options: Scrambles it so it cannot be understood without the key
Deletes it after it is sent
Compresses it to make it smaller

questions.solution: Encryption scrambles data so that only someone with the key can understand it
questions.hint: It protects data even if it is intercepted

questions.text: What is the difference between a LAN and a WAN?

options: A LAN covers a small area such as one building; a WAN covers a large geographical area
A LAN covers a large area; a WAN covers a small area
A LAN is always wireless; a WAN is always wired
A LAN uses the internet; a WAN never does

questions.solution: A LAN covers a small area such as a school; a WAN covers a large area, such as the internet
questions.hint: Think about what 'local' and 'wide' mean

questions.text: Which network topology connects every device to one central switch? Give the name.

feedback.mesh: In a mesh topology devices connect to each other directly
feedback.mesh topology: In a mesh topology devices connect to each other directly

questions.solution: In a star topology every device has its own cable to a central switch
questions.hint: Drawn on paper, the cables spread out from the centre like the points of a shape in the sky

questions.text: Which type of malware copies itself and spreads across a network on its own, without the user opening a file?

feedback: A virus needs an infected file to be opened or run
A Trojan relies on the user installing it
Adware shows unwanted adverts

questions.solution: A worm replicates itself and spreads through networks without needing a host file or user action
questions.hint: It wriggles through the network by itself

questions.text: Which protocol is used to transfer web pages securely, using encryption? Give the abbreviation.

feedback.http: HTTP is not encrypted: the secure version has an extra letter
feedback.ftp: FTP transfers files, not secure web pages

questions.solution: HTTPS (hypertext transfer protocol secure) encrypts web pages as they are sent
questions.hint: It is the normal web protocol with S (for secure) on the end

questions.text: Which address is assigned to a device's network interface card by the manufacturer and does not normally change?

feedback: An IP address is given to a device by the network and can change
A URL identifies a web page
An email address identifies a mailbox, not a device

questions.solution: A MAC address is set by the manufacturer and identifies the network interface card
questions.hint: It is fixed in the hardware

questions.text: Which of these is a valid IPv4 address?

feedback: Each part of an IPv4 address must be from 0 to 255
An IPv4 address has four numbers
An IPv4 address has exactly four numbers

questions.solution: An IPv4 address is four numbers from 0 to 255 separated by dots
questions.hint: Count the numbers and check each one is no more than 255

questions.text: What is the name for a set of rules that devices must follow to communicate over a network? Give the word.
questions.solution: A protocol is a set of rules for communication, for example HTTP or TCP/IP
questions.hint: HTTP, FTP and SMTP are all examples

questions.text: An attacker types database code into a website's login box to get data out of the database. What is this attack called?
questions.solution: Typing SQL code into an input box so the database runs it is SQL injection
questions.hint: The code is injected into the database query

questions.text: A website receives so much traffic from an attacker that real users cannot reach it. Give the name of this type of attack.
questions.solution: A denial of service (DoS) attack floods a server with traffic so that real users are denied the service
questions.hint: Think about what the flood of traffic does for the genuine users of the website

questions.text: A hacker uses a program that tries every possible password until one works. Which attack is this?
questions.solution: Trying every possible combination is a brute force attack; long passwords and lockouts make it harder
questions.hint: It relies on trying again and again, not on cleverness

questions.text: Which protocol is used to send emails from a device to a mail server?

feedback: HTTP transfers web pages
FTP transfers files
HTTPS transfers web pages securely

questions.solution: SMTP (simple mail transfer protocol) sends emails
questions.hint: The M stands for mail

questions.text: Which network device forwards data packets between different networks, for example between a home network and the internet? Give the name.

feedback.switch: A switch connects devices within one network
feedback.hub: A hub connects devices within one network

questions.solution: A router forwards packets between networks, using IP addresses
questions.hint: It chooses the route that packets take

questions.text: In a full mesh network, what happens if one cable fails?

options: Data can take another route, so the network keeps working
Only the central switch keeps working

questions.solution: In a mesh network devices have several connections, so data can be sent another way
questions.hint: How many routes are there between two devices in a mesh?

questions.text: Someone watches over a person's shoulder as they type their PIN at a cash machine. What is this called?
questions.solution: Watching someone enter a PIN or password is shoulder surfing, a form of social engineering
questions.hint: The name describes where the person is looking from

questions.text: A school wants to stop staff opening attachments in fake emails. Which measure deals most directly with this threat?

options: Training staff to recognise phishing emails

questions.solution: Fake emails are phishing, and the most direct defence is teaching staff to spot them
questions.hint: The threat relies on people being tricked

questions.text: Which of these helps to prevent SQL injection?

options: Validating user input before it is used in a database query

questions.solution: Checking (validating and sanitising) input before it reaches a query helps to stop attackers running their own SQL
questions.hint: The attack comes through what users type in

questions.text: Which type of malware encrypts a user's files and demands payment to unlock them? Give the term.
questions.solution: Ransomware encrypts files and demands a ransom; backups help a victim recover without paying
questions.hint: It holds the files to ransom

questions.text: A file is sent across the internet in packets. Which statement is correct?

options: Packets can take different routes and are put back in order at the destination
All packets must take exactly the same route
Each packet contains the whole file

questions.solution: Each packet is numbered, may travel by a different route, and is reassembled in order at the destination
questions.hint: Each packet carries a sequence number

questions.text: What is the main job of the Domain Name System (DNS)?

options: To turn a domain name such as www.example.com into an IP address
To give devices their MAC addresses

questions.solution: DNS looks up the IP address that matches a domain name, so the browser can contact the right server
questions.hint: Computers find servers by number, but people type names

questions.text: A bank asks for your password and also sends a one-time code to your phone that you must type in. Give the name of this security method.
questions.solution: Needing two different things (a password and a code on your phone) is two-factor authentication
questions.hint: Count the separate things you must provide

questions.text: Compared with a wired connection, a disadvantage of Wi-Fi is that it…

options: is usually slower and can suffer from interference
needs a cable to every device

questions.solution: Wireless signals are usually slower than cables and can be weakened by walls and interference
questions.hint: Think about walls and other signals

questions.text: A company's star network has a central switch. Which statement is accurate?

options: If one computer's cable fails, only that computer loses its connection
If any cable fails, the whole network stops
The switch sends all data to every device

questions.solution: Each device has its own cable to the switch, so one broken cable only affects that device (but a failed switch affects all)
questions.hint: Each computer has its own cable to the centre

questions.text: Which statement about encryption is accurate?

options: Encrypted data can still be intercepted, but it cannot be understood without the key
Encryption stops data from being intercepted
Encrypted data cannot be sent over the internet

questions.solution: Encryption does not stop interception; it makes intercepted data unreadable without the key
questions.hint: Think about what a hacker sees if they intercept encrypted data

questions.text: What does a firewall protect a school network from?

options: Unauthorised access from outside the network

questions.solution: A firewall filters traffic between the network and the outside, blocking unauthorised access
questions.hint: It sits between the school network and the internet

questions.text: What is penetration testing used for?

options: Finding weaknesses in a system by simulating an attack, so they can be fixed
Checking that cables are plugged in
Encrypting every file on a server

questions.solution: Penetration testers are allowed to try to break in, to find weaknesses before real attackers do
questions.hint: Testers act like attackers, with permission

questions.text: A user types the correct web address but is redirected to a fake copy of the website that collects their login details. Give the name of this attack.

feedback.phishing: Phishing uses fake emails or messages; here the user typed the right address and was redirected

questions.solution: Redirecting users from a genuine web address to a fake website is pharming
questions.hint: It sounds like a word for growing crops, and it is related to phishing

questions.text: Why are files split into packets before being sent over a network?

options: Packets can travel by different routes, and only lost packets need to be sent again
Packets make data impossible to intercept
Packets remove the need for IP addresses
Packets must all travel in order along one route

questions.solution: Small packets can take the least busy routes, and if one is lost only that packet is resent
questions.hint: Think about what happens when part of the data is lost

questions.text: Which data type stores a whole number, such as 42?

feedback: A real (float) has a decimal part
A Boolean is True or False
A character is a single letter or symbol

questions.solution: An integer is a whole number; a real (float) has a decimal part
questions.hint: Think of the data type for counting things

questions.text: Which search algorithm checks each item in a list one by one, from the start, until it finds the target? Give the name.

feedback.binary search: A binary search keeps halving a sorted list
feedback.binary: A binary search keeps halving a sorted list

questions.solution: A linear search checks each item in turn from the start
questions.hint: It goes along the list in a straight line

questions.text: Which data type can only hold the values True or False?
questions.solution: A Boolean holds one of two values: True or False
questions.hint: It is named after the mathematician George Boole

questions.text: What is iteration?

options: Repeating a set of instructions, for example with a loop
Making a decision with an if statement
Running instructions one after another in order
feedback: That is selection
That is sequence

questions.solution: Iteration means repeating instructions, using a for loop or a while loop
questions.hint: Think about loops

questions.text: Which data type would you use to store a name such as 'Priya'? Give the name of the data type.

feedback.character: A character is only a single letter; a name is several
feedback.char: A character is only a single letter; a name is several

questions.solution: Text made of several characters is stored as a string
questions.hint: Think of a row of characters joined together, like beads on a thread

questions.text: What is an algorithm?

options: A step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem

questions.solution: An algorithm is a sequence of steps that solves a problem; it can be written as pseudocode or a flowchart
questions.hint: A recipe is a kind of one

questions.text: Which statement about binary search is correct?

options: The list must be sorted before a binary search can be used
It checks every item in order from the start
It only works on unsorted lists
It is always slower than a linear search

questions.solution: Binary search compares with the middle item and throws away half the list each time, so the list must be in order
questions.hint: Binary search decides which half to keep: what must be true for that to work?

questions.text: Which sorting algorithm repeatedly compares pairs of adjacent items and swaps them if they are in the wrong order? Give the name.

feedback.merge sort: Merge sort splits and merges lists
feedback.insertion sort: Insertion sort inserts each item into a sorted part of the list

questions.solution: Bubble sort compares adjacent pairs and swaps them, so large values 'bubble' to the end
questions.hint: The largest values rise to the end like bubbles in water

questions.text: Which sorting algorithm splits a list into single items and then merges them back together in order?
questions.solution: Merge sort splits the list into single items, then merges pairs of sorted lists until one sorted list is left
questions.hint: The name describes how the lists are joined back together

questions.text: What is the name for checking that data entered follows sensible rules, such as an age being between 0 and 120? Give the term.

feedback.verification: Verification checks that data has been copied or typed correctly, for example by entering it twice

questions.solution: Validation checks that data is sensible and follows rules; it cannot check that the data is actually correct
questions.hint: It checks that data is valid, not that it is true

questions.text: In Python, what does 17 % 5 give?

feedback: That is 17 // 5 (integer division)
That is 17 / 5
That is 17 * 5

questions.solution: % gives the remainder: 17 = 3 × 5 + 2, so 17 % 5 = 2
questions.hint: In Python, % is the modulus operator

questions.text: Which kind of loop is most suitable when you know in advance exactly how many times the code must repeat?

options: A count-controlled loop, such as for
A condition-controlled loop, such as while

questions.solution: A count-controlled (for) loop repeats a fixed number of times
questions.hint: The loop counts the repeats for you

questions.text: Breaking a large problem down into smaller sub-problems that are easier to solve is called what? Give the term.
questions.solution: Decomposition breaks a problem into smaller parts that can be solved one at a time
questions.hint: It means taking something apart into its pieces

questions.text:
What is printed by this Python code?
total = 0
for i in range(1, 5):
    total = total + i
print(total)
questions.solution: range(1, 5) gives 1, 2, 3 and 4 (not 5), so total = 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10
questions.hint: range(1, 5) stops before 5: list the values of i first

questions.text: A binary search looks for 23 in the sorted list 3, 8, 12, 17, 23, 30, 41. Which item is checked first?

feedback: A binary search starts with the middle item, not the target
That is where a linear search would start
12 is not the middle of 7 items

questions.solution: There are 7 items, so the middle one (the 4th) is checked first: 17
questions.hint: A binary search starts in the middle of the list

feedback.small: 7 > 5 is True, so the if branch runs

questions.solution: 7 > 5 is True, so the code in the if branch runs and prints big
questions.hint: Is 7 greater than 5?

questions.text: After one complete pass of a bubble sort into ascending order, what does the list 5, 1, 4, 2, 8 become?

feedback: That is the fully sorted list: one pass is not enough here
That is after only the first comparison and swap
Some swaps happen during the pass

questions.solution: Swap 5 and 1, swap 5 and 4, swap 5 and 2, then 5 and 8 stay: 1, 4, 2, 5, 8
questions.hint: Compare each adjacent pair from left to right, swapping when the left one is bigger

questions.text: Which validation check makes sure that a field has not been left empty?

feedback: A range check makes sure a value is between limits
A length check counts the characters
A format check makes sure data follows a pattern

questions.solution: A presence check makes sure something has been entered
questions.hint: The check makes sure data is there

questions.text: In Python, what is the value of 17 // 5?
questions.solution: // is integer division: 17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2, so 17 // 5 = 3
questions.hint: // divides and throws away the remainder

questions.text: In an SQL query, which keyword names the table that the data comes from?

feedback: SELECT lists the fields to return
WHERE filters the records
ORDER BY sorts the results

questions.solution: FROM names the table, for example SELECT name FROM students
questions.hint: Look at SELECT name … students: which word goes in the gap?

questions.text:
What does this Python code print?
n = 3
while n > 0:
    print(n)
    n = n - 1

options: 3, 2 and 1, each on a new line
3, 2, 1 and 0, each on a new line
1, 2 and 3, each on a new line
feedback: When n becomes 0, the condition n > 0 is False, so 0 is not printed
n starts at 3 and goes down
n > 0 is True at the start, so the loop runs

questions.solution: It prints 3, then 2, then 1; when n reaches 0 the condition n > 0 is False and the loop stops
questions.hint: Write a trace table for n and check the condition each time

questions.text: A linear search looks for 9 in the list 4, 7, 1, 9, 3, 6. How many items does it check, including the one it finds?
questions.solution: It checks 4, 7, 1 and then 9: 4 items
questions.hint: Start at the first item and count until you reach the target

questions.text: Which validation check would make sure a UK postcode is typed in a pattern such as LL9 9LL? Give the name of the check.

feedback.length check: A length check only counts the characters, not the pattern
feedback.range check: A range check is for numbers between limits

questions.solution: A format check makes sure data follows a pattern of letters and digits
questions.hint: The data must follow a particular pattern

questions.text: A binary search is used on a sorted list of 1000 items. At most, roughly how many items does it need to check?
questions.solution: Each check halves the list: 1000 → 500 → 250 → … → 1 takes about 10 halvings (2 to the power 10 = 1024)
questions.hint: Each check halves the number of items left

questions.text: Which is an advantage of merge sort compared with bubble sort?

options: It is usually much faster for large lists
It only works on lists that are already sorted
feedback: Merge sort usually needs extra memory for the sub-lists
Bubble sort is simpler to program

questions.solution: Merge sort is much more efficient on large lists, although it uses more memory and is harder to program
questions.hint: Think about a list of a million items

questions.text: What is the name for a table used to record the values of variables as a program runs, line by line? Give the term.

feedback.truth table: A truth table shows the outputs of a logic circuit

questions.solution: A trace table records the value of each variable as each line runs, which helps to find errors
questions.hint: You follow (trace) the program step by step

questions.text:
What does this Python code print?
words = ['cat', 'dog', 'emu']
print(words[1])

feedback: Python lists start at index 0, so cat is words[0]
emu is words[2]
Index 1 exists in a list of 3 items

questions.solution: Python lists are indexed from 0, so words[1] is the second item: dog
questions.hint: In Python, the first item of a list has index 0

questions.text: An insertion sort is putting 3, 7, 5, 2 into ascending order. What does the list look like just after 5 has been inserted into place?
questions.solution: 3 and 7 are already in order; 5 is inserted between them to give 3, 5, 7, and 2 has not been moved yet
questions.hint: Insertion sort builds a sorted part on the left one item at a time

questions.text: When must a linear search be used instead of a binary search?

options: When the list is not sorted
When the list is very large and sorted
When the list is in alphabetical order

questions.solution: Binary search only works on a sorted list, so an unsorted list needs a linear search (or must be sorted first)
questions.hint: What does binary search need to be true about the list?

questions.text:
This Python code should add up the numbers 1 to 10, but the answer is wrong.
total = 0
for i in range(1, 10):
    total = total + i
print(total)
What is the error?

options: range(1, 10) stops at 9, so 10 is never added
print should be inside the loop

questions.solution: range(1, 10) gives 1 to 9, so the total is 45; it should be range(1, 11) to include 10 (total 55)
questions.hint: Write out the values that range(1, 10) gives

questions.text: A program keeps asking for a password until the correct one is entered. Which construct is most suitable?
questions.solution: The number of attempts is not known in advance, so a while loop that checks a condition is needed
questions.hint: Do you know in advance how many attempts there will be?

questions.text: A missing bracket stops a program from being translated and run at all. What type of error is this? Give the term.

feedback.logic error: A program with a logic error still runs, but gives the wrong result
feedback.logical error: A program with a logic error still runs, but gives the wrong result

questions.solution: Breaking the rules of the language, such as a missing bracket, is a syntax error
questions.hint: The code breaks the grammar rules of the language

questions.text: Which statement about logic errors is accurate?

options: The program runs but gives the wrong result
The program will not run at all
They are always found by the translator

questions.solution: With a logic error the program runs but does the wrong thing, so testing is needed to find it
questions.hint: Would a translator know what result you wanted?

questions.text:
What does this Python code print?
x = 10
y = 3
print(x // y + x % y)

feedback: That is only x // y: add x % y too
That is only x % y: add x // y too
That is x + y

questions.solution: x // y = 3 and x % y = 1, so 3 + 1 = 4
questions.hint: Work out x // y and x % y separately
